guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Adult Basic Life Support 2021
title: Adult cardiac arrest from electrocution
setting: Amateur dramatic theatre show. 24M lighting crew member collapsed after receiving an electric shock from a faulty appliance. Lying still, unresponsive.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive and not breathing normally after a sudden collapse. This is cardiac arrest, a critical life-threatening emergency. Unequivocally sick: start CPR and use an AED.

shared.danger: Faulty appliance (electricity source has been isolated and safe to approach)
shared.circulation: No effective pulse, electrical burns on entry/exit sites

history.history: Shocked by faulty stage light, collapsed immediately
history.injuries: Electrical burn entry wound to hand and exit wound to knee

followUp.question: What is your immediate priority action after ensuring safety?

options.text: Start chest compressions, call 999, and attach the AED as soon as available
Treat the electrical burn wounds on the hand and knee with cold water
Place in the recovery position and monitor his asthma
Give 2 rescue breaths only and wait for the ambulance

followUp.explanation: Cardiac arrest from electrocution requires immediate CPR and defibrillation. Burn care is secondary to preserving life. The recovery position is only for responsive or breathing patients.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Ensure the electrical source is safe and isolated before touching the patient. Start CPR 30:2 immediately.
levelFlags.erNotes: Deliver high-quality CPR, manage the airway with basic airway adjuncts and high-flow oxygen, attach AED, and treat burns after resuscitation starts.
